title: Die Walküre
subtitle: Hofmann, Bode, Salminen · Boulez
summary: Complete Die Walküre from the Bayreuth Festival's centenary Ring (Chéreau production, Boulez conducting). It is most likely the premiere on 25 July 1976, the only 1976 Walküre known to have been broadcast or recorded. This copy appears to be Opera Depot's 3-CD issue OD 10747-3 (39 tracks, 2012).
date_evidence: Folder '76 Walk Bayreuth' and album tag 'Die Walküre - Bayreuth, '76' give only the year. The 1976 Walküre was given on 25 July and 5, 13 and 22 Aug (s1). Wagnerdisco's list of all known Bayreuth recordings names only one 1976 Walküre source: the 25 July premiere broadcast (s7; re-read by the reconciler). The tags name McIntyre, which rules out 5 Aug (Hans Sotin was Wotan, s1). The Opera Depot cast has Salminen as Hunding (s3), and Ridderbusch replaced him on 5, 13 and 22 Aug (s1, s5), which leaves 25 July. Wagnerdisco gives this cast and the OD label for the 25 July 1976 broadcast (s2). The files have 39 tracks, as OD 10747-3 does (OD splits the acts 14/12/13; this copy splits the discs 16/10/13), and the tags carry 2012, the OD issue year. The date stays inferred: the insert PDF, which may state it, was not read (the reconciler had no NAS access), and no one has listened to the recording.
broadcaster: Bayerischer Rundfunk (live festival broadcast; the broadcaster is presumed, not confirmed from a listing)

Unresolved; leaning Randová. For Eva Randová: wagnerdisco's 25 July 1976 broadcast entry (s2) and the Opera Depot OD 10747-3 cast and description (s3), but these two are not independent, because s2 lists the OD release. For Yvonne Minton (Q437381): the festival DB's 1976 Walküre cast (s1) and its Walküre Fricka role page (s10), 1976 Minton and 1977 Randová, neither with a replacement; Wikipedia's Jahrhundertring cast table (s8), which is production-level and probably drawn from the DB; and Minton's biography (s6), which has her 'taking on Fricka in Das Rheingold and Die Walküre' in 1976. Points towards Randová on 25 July: the festival DB's own Rheingold role page (s4) lists Randová as the regular 1976 Fricka, with Minton as replacement only on 4 and 21 Aug, the Rheingolds of cycles 2 and 4. Both the OD Rheingold release (s11) and wagnerdisco's 24 July 1976 Rheingold broadcast entry (s12) list Randová as Fricka. A plausible reading is that the two women shared Fricka in both operas: Randová in cycles 1 and 3 (25 July and 13 Aug), Minton in cycles 2 and 4 (5 and 22 Aug). The DB's Walküre record may simply omit that replacement. This is inference; no source names the 25 July Fricka apart from the OD release. Randová is a Czech mezzo, Minton an Australian mezzo with a different timbre, so listening to Act II, Scene 1 should settle it.

open_questions: Fricka: Eva Randová or Yvonne Minton? Only the OD release (and wagnerdisco, which lists it) names Randová for 25 July. The festival DB's Walküre record names only Minton. The festival's Rheingold record shows the two sharing Fricka in 1976, with Randová in cycles 1 and 3, which favors Randová for 25 July. Listen to Act II, Scene 1 (Disc 1 track 16 to Disc 2 track 2) and compare with known Randová and Minton recordings, or read the insert PDF.

The date assumes this copy is the OD 10747-3 issue or the same 25 July broadcast (39 tracks, 2012 tag, Hofmann/McIntyre in tags). Read 'Walkuere - Insert.pdf' for the label, catalogue number and stated date; the reconciler had no NAS access and did not read it.
Hunding: Salminen (25 July) vs Ridderbusch (all three August dates) is the audible check that pins the date if the insert doesn't. Disc 1 tracks 4 and 7.

No contemporary review of the 25 July 1976 Walküre and no BR broadcast listing were read. The web-search budget ran out during reconciliation. Reviews of the premiere week (Opera, Der Spiegel, FAZ, Süddeutsche) could confirm Fricka.
Act timings from durations: Act I 63.7 min, Act II 88.0 min, Act III 66.3 min. No one has listened to check for announcements or applause; the last track (5.5 min) may include closing applause.
Wikidata QIDs not found or not checked for Irja Auroora, Adelheid Krauss, Katie Clarke, Ilse Gramatzki, Elisabeth Glauser and Jacques Schmidt.
Codex did not run (usage limit), so this record rests on one researcher's work plus the reconciler's re-checks; it was not independently cross-checked.
